meta.title: The one list
meta.authority: This file is the ONLY record of what is done. Prose docs explain the work; they do not track it.
meta.howToRead:
pnpm backlog          — the working view (open + blocked)
pnpm backlog --lane owner — one lane
pnpm check:backlog    — prove every row against the tree (runs in CI)
rules: A row's status is proven by its verify probe, not by memory. If they disagree, CI fails.
A probe must measure the CONSEQUENCE in the tree, never restate the row's own title. A probe that passes by existing is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs.
Manual rows never fail the build (ADR-970). They carry evidence + a checked date and go stale loudly.
Parked rows are not probed: 'you could do this now' is true of everything parked and therefore says nothing.
Never delete a probe to make CI pass. That is precisely how the previous five master lists drifted.

lanes.owner: Config or a decision. No code unblocks it.
lanes.program: A named multi-phase program. Needs a scheduling decision, not a start.
lanes.hygiene: Debt in the record or the instruments.

entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18 by an owner decision, after the row rescoped from three clicks to one question. 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY, BY OBSERVATION. This row was closed claiming TWO of the three were already done. Only ONE was. check:contrast genuinely blocks - it sits in ci.yml's guards array inside the checks job, so requiring it separately would be a second name for the same gate. THE pr-compare CLAIM WAS FALSE, and it was taken from prose: .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml asserts in its first line that pr-compare is a REQUIRED status context, citing ruleset 17640795. PR #2161 disproved it by merging. Auto-merge fired at 21:45:31 while the pr-compare check run was still in_progress (it completed success at 21:52:50), and the merged SHA carried exactly one commit status, Vercel's - so no substitute pr-compare status stood in for it. A context that is required cannot be pending at merge. See LIVE-049. The irony is the point: this row was closed by citing a sentence in a file, hours after ADR-1082 made 're-test the premise, do not trust the prose' a rule in AGENTS.md. THE THIRD WAS A DECISION, NOT A TASK, and the owner made it: check:adoption STAYS ADVISORY. ci.yml's own twenty-line rationale carried the argument (ADR-970): it is a SCOREBOARD of design-debt COUNTS, a count ratchet fires on legitimate growth - 'bespoke-cards: 0 means adding any new *-card.tsx fails a PR that has nothing to do with the design system' - and an advisory finding forced through a blocking gate teaches everyone to route around the gate. THE COST OF THAT CHOICE IS KNOWN AND ACCEPTED, and is written here so the next reader does not have to rediscover it: literal-radius read '🔴 rose' from 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-18 and nobody looked, even though the advisory step already writes the scoreboard into every run's summary. The gate is visible and was still unread; that is an argument about ATTENTION, not about blocking, and the remedy if it recurs is a louder surface (a PR comment rather than a run summary), not a reversal of this decision. Re-open only with new evidence, not with the same argument.

entries.title: DECIDE the amber-button contrast fix: 8 midnight-dark contexts are carried as declared ceilings until then
entries.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-17 in CI, not estimated. The failing pair is WHITE TEXT ON THE AMBER BUTTON, not amber as text: #FFFFFF on #F0AD4E is 1.95:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. Amber as TEXT is fine (#F0AD4E on the midnight-dark surface #161C28 is 8.77:1). 🔴 THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL REMEDY - 'swap to primary-strong' - IS A NO-OP IN MIDNIGHT-DARK. That skin sets --color-primary-strong to #F0AD4E, the SAME value as --color-primary, so the swap changes nothing. It works in midnight-LIGHT, where primary-strong is #8C5410 and white on it measures 6.19:1. Anyone applying the fix as written would see light mode go green, dark mode stay red, and reasonably conclude the guard was flaky. WHY IT SURFACED NOW: LIVE-008 fixed a selector that could never match, so midnight-dark paints its real palette instead of falling back to the generic .dark one. The failure is PRE-EXISTING and was invisible, not introduced. It costs 8 contexts on the a11y ratchet, all midnight-dark desktop, contrast only: /, /about, /discover, /pricing and /the-lab 0 -> 3; /the-quest 0 -> 4; /spaces 2 -> 6; /the-community 3 -> 7. TWO OPTIONS, both measured: (A) keep the brand amber and darken the FOREGROUND on it - #1C2535 on #F0AD4E is 7.90:1, #161C28 is 8.77:1. The brand colour is untouched and only the text on the button moves. (B) give midnight-dark a genuine primary-strong and keep white text - #7A4A0E gives 7.46:1, #8C5410 gives 6.19:1 (the value midnight-light already uses). (A) is the smaller change and preserves the accent exactly; (B) matches how the light skin already solves it. It is a BRAND decision either way, which is why it is not being made in code.

verify.evidence: Measured in CI 2026-08-17 (run 32077367930, `pnpm a11y:baselines`): 8 midnight-dark desktop contexts regressed, contrast only, and the capture REFUSED to raise the baselines rather than laundering the rise. Ratios computed from the tokens in app/globals.css: #FFFFFF on #F0AD4E = 1.95:1; #FFFFFF on #8C5410 = 6.19:1; #1C2535 on #F0AD4E = 7.90:1. Not repo-probeable: which remedy to take is a brand decision, and a probe asserting either one would force a choice the owner has not made.

entries.notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-18: WAIVE FOR NOW. The eight midnight-dark desktop contrast contexts are declared CEILINGS in test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json (/, /about, /discover, /pricing, /the-lab at 3; /the-quest 4; /spaces 6; /the-community 7), each carrying the measurement, both remedies, and the exact command that converts it back to a reading at 0. check:a11y-baselines prints every one of them on EVERY run - 'every ceiling is headroom a real regression can sit in while this prints a tick' - so the debt is carried in the open rather than hidden. This unblocks pr-compare without laundering a WCAG failure into a recorded fact. 🔴 THE ROW IS BLOCKED, NOT DONE. A known 1.95:1 pair is live in production on the amber button in midnight-dark. Both fixes are measured and one line each: (A) #1C2535 on #F0AD4E = 7.90:1, brand colour untouched; (B) --color-primary-strong #7A4A0E with white = 7.46:1, the shape midnight-LIGHT already uses. Whichever is picked, the eight ceilings retire in the same pass.

entries.title: Lift 8b: a loading prop on IconButton, matching Button's
entries.detail: Icon-only controls are exactly the ones where a tap leaves no other evidence it landed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='components/ui/icon-button.tsx',T='components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(T))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8'),test=fs.readFileSync(T,'utf8');const cut=src.indexOf('export function IconLink');if(cut<0)process.exit(79);const B=src.slice(0,cut),L=src.slice(cut);function a(s,k){let i=0;while((i=s.indexOf(k+'={',i))>=0){const aria=s.slice(Math.max(0,i-5),i).endsWith('aria-');const e=s.indexOf('}',i);if(e>0&&s.slice(i,e).includes('loading')&&(k.indexOf('aria-')===0||!aria))return true;i+=k.length}return false}const bad=[];if(!a(B,'disabled'))bad.push('IconButton does not disable while loading; a second tap re-fires the action');if(!a(B,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconButton does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-disabled'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-disabled while loading');if(!a(L,'aria-busy'))bad.push('IconLink does not set aria-busy while loading');if(!test.includes('does not fire the handler again'))bad.push('the double-fire assertion is gone from '+T);if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /loading/` in the component, which passes because the WORD appears anywhere in the file, including in a comment describing the prop it is supposed to be proving. Replaced with the consequence: IconButton must disable while loading (so a second tap cannot re-fire the action) and set aria-busy; IconLink must use the aria pair INSTEAD of the real `disabled`, because a real disabled drops it out of the tab order mid-navigation; and the double-fire assertion must still exist in the test file. ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: both controls live in one file and the string 'aria-disabled=' CONTAINS 'disabled=', so an unscoped regex let each component satisfy the other's check. Two of four deliberate breaks passed before that was caught, which is exactly why a probe is not trusted until it has been seen to fail. It now splits the file at IconLink and judges each half alone; all four breaks fire. A SECOND trap cost another round: the first scoped version used a regex, and this string travels JSON -> shell -> `node -e`, where a lone backslash does not survive intact - "\\b" arrived as a literal BACKSPACE, so every check silently matched nothing and the row read as regressed. The probe is now backslash-free, scanning with indexOf instead of RegExp, and was re-proved through the guard's own shell rather than only standalone.

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. entries.detail: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18, and the row changed shape rather than closing. THE SYMPTOM IS GONE: three consecutive production builds (18:46, 19:01, 19:09) uploaded 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling and every one logged 'Restored build cache from previous deployment'. No invalidation line anywhere. The 1.53 GB reading the row was filed on does not reproduce. WHAT IS STILL TRUE is the second half of the original row: nothing PREVENTS a recurrence. scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs was written for exactly that on 2026-08-17 and has never run on a real build. It was wired into postbuild in #2159 and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge, because the preview build of that change printed what no amount of reading could: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' THE FLOOR ARM WAS RIGHT (node_modules 933 MiB, 27% clear of its 1.25 GiB budget, exactly as predicted). THE TRIM ARM IS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE WRONG QUANTITY: measure() sums RAW BYTES ON DISK and Vercel's ceiling applies to the PACKED archive. Raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1, not the ~3% the script's header assumes, because the Turbopack cache compresses hard and is the dominant term. Wired as-is it would delete a 1.5 GiB compiler cache on EVERY build to prevent an overflow that is not happening, turning a working warm cache into a guaranteed cold compile forever. TO CLOSE: fix the calibration (LIVE-048), then wire the gate in the SAME change as a preview build that prints it green. Do NOT close this row by deleting the guard or by declaring the symptom gone: the symptom being gone is why there is time to get the instrument right, not a reason to skip it.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1070). check:authz was FILE-level: it saw a gate called somewhere in the file, so an early return before the gate, a gate on one branch of an if, and a gated GET beside an ungated POST all read as green. It now requires EVERY exported HTTP method to pass three structural rules, following the body through a wrapper's local handler (27 cron routes) and into file-local helpers: R1 per-export, R2 the gate is not nested inside if/else/switch/catch, R3 no createAdminClient() query above the gate. R3 IS A DELIBERATE NARROWING AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. A literal 'any return before the gate' rule was tried against the real corpus first: it fires on 10 of the 52 gated handlers and all ten are validation (400 on a malformed body, 429 on rate limit, an empty list for a blank query). Shipping that would have been 100% false positives on day one, which is the ADR-970 shape - a guard that cannot fire honestly gets routed around and then reads as coverage. What is dangerous is not returning early, it is answering from the service-role client before you know who is asking, and that is what R3 measures. IT FOUND THREE REAL FALSE GREENS, each re-verdicted as a digest-pinned human reading: check-handle (auth.getUser inside an if, over a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) -> public; auth/callback (auth.getUser three branches deep in a swallowed analytics block; the real credential check is exchangeCodeForSession) -> token-credential; q/[slug] (service-role read of the code row before getMyProfileId, which answers WHO scanned, not MAY they) -> self-scoped. entries.title: Two eyebrow registers exist and neither is wrong: pick the one that wins
entries.detail: Surfaced by LIVE-025, and it is a design decision rather than a refactor, which is why it is not being made in code. There are TWO eyebrow implementations and nobody reconciled them. (1) app/globals.css locks the `eyebrow` utility at 0.75rem / 0.18em / bold, and 87 sites use it. (2) components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx exports an <Eyebrow> component with about 26 adopters rendering text-body-sm, 0.875rem - which is DAWN's DECLARED eyebrow size, i.e. precisely the half of the DAWN split that globals.css resolved DOWN to 0.75rem on 2026-08-05. So the block kit is not drifting by accident; it is rendering the value DAWN published, and the CSS is rendering the value this repo chose instead. Beyond those two there is a third de-facto register: 615 sites pair uppercase with a literal tracking, dominated by an 11px `text-2xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`, and many of those are pill badges and dense table headers where 0.18em would widen the label past the pill that was sized to fit it. entries.title: One dropped TCP connection during prerender kills the whole deploy, and nothing retries
entries.detail: OBSERVED, not theorised. The preview build of 656dac3 failed while the PRODUCTION build of the SAME COMMIT succeeded four minutes earlier. The failure: `TypeError: fetch failed / Caused by: Error: read ECONNRESET` on a Supabase read, which the reader wraps as DiscoverReadError and rethrows, and Next reports 'Export encountered an error on /discover/events/[slug]/page: breathe-connect-expand-2026-09-10, exiting the build.' One transient reset on one slug ended the export. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLAKY PREVIEW: `main` is protected and MERGING DEPLOYS TO PRODUCTION (AGENTS.md). This same read runs during the production export, so the same blip takes down a production deploy, and the only evidence would be a stack trace that looks like a code fault. The build is otherwise healthy - the report says 'No memory or disk space problems detected'. THE FIX IS NOT A BARE try/catch. Swallowing the error would silently ship a /discover with missing events, which is the fail-safe-with-no-gate pattern AGENTS.md names ('every fail-safe needs a gate that notices it fired'). The honest shape is a bounded retry with backoff around the read for RETRYABLE transport faults only (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, fetch failed), leaving a genuine query error - bad SQL, RLS denial, missing column - fatal exactly as it is now. If a retry is exhausted the build should still fail, loudly, with the slug named. A count of retries consumed belongs in the build log so a rising number is visible before it becomes an outage.

The observed killer arrived RESOLVED, not thrown - supabase-js catches the fetch rejection and resolves with a synthetic error whose message carries the network cause - so the retry decision reads the error's SHAPE: network-ish (fetch failed/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/...) retries, a Postgres/PostgREST code never does, and empty data is NEVER retried (a detail-route empty result is a believed 404; retry-until-it-exists turns 404s into timeouts). Call sites pass thunks so each attempt builds a fresh PostgrestBuilder - re-awaiting one builder re-reads its settled failure. lib/discover.test.ts proves the retry FIRES (two transient failures then success = three calls) and REFUSES (deterministic error = one call), per the watch-it-fail rule.

Same stale-blocker shape as LIVE-012, found the same way - by reading the code before acting on the row. entries.title: The check:backlog cost ceiling is asserted on wall clock, so a loaded box fails it instead of a slow probe
entries.detail: OBSERVED 2026-08-18, once, in a full `pnpm test` run: 'check:backlog took 23.8s, over its 20s budget. Something added expensive work to a probe.' Nothing had. MEASURED on the same tree, unloaded: origin/main 13.38s and 13.39s, the branch under test 13.49s and 13.50s. Three probes added that day (OWN-029, LIVE-029, LIVE-035, all single-file reads) cost about 110 ms between them, 0.8%, against 6.5s of headroom. A second full run of the identical tree passed. THE ASSERTION MEASURES THE WRONG QUANTITY. It spawns check:backlog and times its WALL CLOCK, from inside a suite that is at that moment running 838 test files across 4 cores. What it reads is contention, and contention is not a property of any probe. Its own message then sends the next reader hunting for expensive work that does not exist, and tells them - correctly, for the failure it was designed for - that raising the number is not the fix. So the honest failure mode and the noisy one are indistinguishable, on the one gate whose whole job is telling those two apart. The budget itself is right and should stay: LIVE-034 closed a real 24s regression and the ceiling is what stopped it recurring. What needs to change is the CLOCK. Measure the guard's CPU time rather than its elapsed time, or run this one assertion outside the parallel pool. NOT A FIX: raising GUARD_BUDGET_MS, which would blind the gate to the growth it exists to catch.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(s.indexOf('GUARD_BUDGET_MS')<0)process.exit(79);if(!/cpuUsage|GUARD_BUDGET_CPU|loadInvariant|process\\.hrtime\\.bigint\\(\\)[\\s\\S]{0,400}cpu/i.test(s)){console.error('the check:backlog budget is still asserted on wall clock, so it fails on a loaded box rather than on an expensive probe');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: check:cache-budget's trim killed two builds: wrong threshold units, and it can delete the fetch cache
entries.detail: MEASURED, not suspected. The gate was wired into postbuild in #2159 and its preview build printed: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' The wiring was reverted before merge. THE DEFECT: measure() sums raw bytes on disk; Vercel's 1.50 GB ceiling applies to the packed archive. On the same tree, raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1. The script's header asserts the two 'have run ~3% apart', and that sentence is the whole bug - everything downstream of it is arithmetic. Turbopack's cache compresses hard and is the dominant term, so the error scales with the half that grows. CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED, and it is worse than 'builds get slower'. The one trim this gate ever ran emptied .next/cache on claude/cache-gate, and the NEXT TWO BUILDS ON THAT BRANCH BOTH DIED: each compiled in ~2.4 minutes and then hung in 'Collecting page data using 3 workers', hitting BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME at 46 minutes. Every other build that day was green, including four production deploys. A CONTROL separated the two suspects: claude/build-pin carried the identical vercel.json buildCommand line and nothing else, on a branch cut from main so its build restored a healthy cache, and it reported 'Build Completed in /vercel/output [59s]'. 59 seconds against two dead builds. The pin is exonerated; the emptied cache is the cause. A SECOND DEFECT, and it is the one that makes this M rather than S: .next/cache is not only Turbopack's compiler cache, it also holds the INCREMENTAL FETCH CACHE. Page-data collection prerenders hundreds of routes that each read Supabase; warm those reads are local, cold every one goes to the network and the build never finishes. The trim drops directories BIGGEST-FIRST rather than by name - deliberately, so a future growth elsewhere is still caught - and that generality is exactly what lets it delete the half the build cannot proceed without. Fixing the threshold is necessary and NOT sufficient: whatever the number becomes, the trim must drop the compiler cache BY NAME or drop nothing. The floor arm is unaffected and was correct: node_modules 933 MiB against 1.25 GiB. TO CLOSE, BOTH HALVES. (a) Make the trim drop only what is safe to lose - name the compiler cache rather than sorting by size - so a firing trim can never take the fetch cache with it. (b) Express the trim point in the units Vercel applies. Measuring the packed size means packing, which is not free on a build; the cheaper honest route is a calibration constant derived from SEVERAL real builds - raw measured by this script, packed read off the build log's 'Uploading build cache [N GB]' line - carried in the file with its measurements and its date, so it can be re-checked rather than trusted. Then re-wire under LIVE-035, in the same change as a preview build that prints it green. NOT A FIX: raising TRIM_AT_GIB to a number that happens to stop it firing, which would leave the units wrong and the gate blind at a different size. A NOTE ON THIS ROW'S OWN PROBE, because it made the mistake twice while being written. First it matched the word 'calibration', which the commit had just added to the file's header explaining the bug - a grep that passes by existing. Rewritten to require a declared CONSTANT, it then matched nothing even with the constant present: it stripped block comments first, and this file's header documents the globs Vercel caches (node_modules/**, .next/cache/**), so a slash next to a star opened a comment that ran to the next close token and blanked the declaration. That is the same defect CORPUS_BASIS strip-comments@2 was written for in the adoption scanner. It now strips line comments only.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(S))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');if(s.indexOf('TRIM_AT_GIB')<0)process.exit(79);const code=s.split('\\n').filter(l=>!/^\\s*(\\/\\/|\\*)/.test(l)).join('\\n');if(!/^\\s*const\\s+[A-Z0-9_]*(PACK|RATIO|CALIBRA)[A-Z0-9_]*\\s*=\\s*[0-9]/m.test(code)){console.error('the trim point is still computed from raw bytes: no declared packed-size constant, only prose');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: pr-compare is not a required check, and the file that said otherwise now records what is
entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18. STEP (a) IS DONE AND IT IS THE ONLY STEP NOBODY IN THE REPO COULD DO: the owner opened ruleset 17640795 and read the required set off the settings page. IT IS FIVE CONTEXTS - checks, analyze, lint, test, Vercel. pr-compare is NOT among them, which confirms the observation this row was filed on: PR #2161 merged on auto-merge at 21:45:31 while its pr-compare check run was still in_progress, finishing green seven minutes after the merge, with exactly one commit status (Vercel's) on the merged SHA. STEP (b): .github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml no longer opens by calling pr-compare REQUIRED. Its header now leads with the reading, the date, the set, and the merge that disproved the old claim, and it keeps the PR #2107 deadlock history in the past tense as the reason the workflow is NOT deleted - the deadlock returns the moment anyone re-requires the context, and this file is what makes that a one-checkbox change. STEP (c): docs/WORKFLOW.md rule 4 now carries the set and is named as the only authority on it, because the whole failure was a workflow comment being cited instead. TWO CONSEQUENCES ARE WRITTEN DOWN THERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE REDISCOVERED. First, 'auto-merge on green' promises compile + lint + typecheck + test + a deployed preview, and promises NOTHING about pixels; a PR that moves rendering is exactly what rule 4 sends to a human. Second, and this was found in the same reading and was not what the row went looking for: 'Require branches to be up to date before merging' is UNCHECKED. A PR merges on the CI it ran against ITS base, not against current main, so two PRs that each pass alone can still break main together. That is a defensible setting for one developer on auto-merge (the alternative serialises every merge behind a fresh run) and it is now a known property with a stated mitigation rather than a surprise. WHAT THIS ROW COST, KEPT HERE ON PURPOSE: it was filed because OWN-004 had been closed hours earlier by citing a sentence in a workflow header, on the same day ADR-1082 made 're-test the premise, never trust the prose' a rule in AGENTS.md. The prose had been wrong since the requirement was removed, and every PR merged on auto-merge that day merged on a narrower gate than the repo's own documentation described.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='.github/workflows/pr-compare-fallback.yml';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');const claims=/REQUIRED .pr-compare. context|is a required status context/.test(s);const read=/RULESET 17640795, read 2026-08-18/.test(s);const set=/required: checks, analyze, lint, test, Vercel\\. NOT pr-compare/.test(s);if(claims){console.error('pr-compare-fallback.yml asserts pr-compare is a required context again; ruleset 17640795 says it is not');process.exit(1)}if(!read||!set){console.error('pr-compare-fallback.yml no longer carries the one-line ruleset reading (date + the five required contexts)');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: Record payment is a one-way money button with no confirm and no undo, and it cost a year tonight
entries.detail: HAPPENED, not hypothesised. The owner pressed 'Record payment' on an active agreement while asking whether they should, and it extended paid_through from 2027-07-27 to 2028-07-27 - claiming a second $490 year the member had not paid. It took a guarded database UPDATE to put back, because THERE IS NO UNDO IN THE UI. TWO THINGS ARE MISSING AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT. (1) NO CONFIRM: the button fires on a single click with no dialog and no before/after, on a field that is money. components/ui/confirm-submit-button.tsx already exists for exactly this and is used on deletes; a renewal is at least as consequential as a delete, and unlike a delete it looks harmless. (2) NO CORRECTION PATH: once an agreement is active the panel renders a read-only summary plus that one button. The paid-through date input exists ONLY on the create form, which is unreachable forever after. So the single control the screen offers is the one that cannot be reversed, and the operator's only exit is a person with database access. WHY IT WILL RECUR IF LEFT: this is a once-a-year action per Space, so nobody builds a habit around it, and the failure is silent - no error, no email, just a wrong date that surfaces when a renewal reminder does not arrive and a member is not asked for money they owe. THE FIX, and the smaller half is the important one: a confirm step naming BOTH dates ('extend Temple of Aset from July 27 2027 to July 27 2028?') would have stopped this outright. An edit path for an active agreement is the second half and can follow. NOT A FIX: a toast after the fact, which tells you what happened without letting you undo it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='components/admin/spaces/manual-agreement-panel.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(s.indexOf('recordPaymentAction')<0)process.exit(79);const guarded=/window\\.confirm|ConfirmSubmitButton|<Dialog|confirm=/.test(s);const editable=/editAgreementAction|updateAgreementAction|correctPaidThrough/.test(s);const missing=[!guarded&&'no confirm step before Record payment',!editable&&'no way to correct an active agreement'].filter(Boolean);if(missing.length){console.error(missing.join('; '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
